text:
sam: Repro'd a nasty steady-state where the batcher waits to fill and the queue climbs -> scheduler keeps delaying, q95 drifts up and we hit client timeouts. We should design a clearer admission/fallback handshake instead of ad-hoc heuristics.
nora: Can you sketch the failure shape you saw?
sam: Short: many small requests from same tenant. Scheduler keeps trying to pack, uses headroom calc which doesn't account for transient KV stalls. Result: long queuing for dozens of reqs. Example log snippet:```
[2024-06-02T09:11:02Z] tenant=payroll enqueue=180 headroom=60 q95_ms=120
[2024-06-02T09:11:04Z] tenant=payroll enqueue=240 headroom=58 q95_ms=220
[2024-06-02T09:11:06Z] tenant=payroll enqueue=310 headroom=55 q95_ms=410
```
eli: Okay. We need an admission signal that is fast and composable. Proposal: scheduler computes an admission_score per-tenant each decision window:
  score = a*queued_p95_ms + b*(kv_miss_rate*1000) + c*cpu_delta_ms - d*headroom_tokens
Trip rule: score > S && queue_len > L -> emit AdmissionAdvice.
hailey: AdmissionAdvice should be explicit: modes = {NORMAL, FASTPATH, EVICT, SOFT_DROP, HARD_DROP}. We avoid HARD_DROP for paid tiers by policy. Also include ttl_ms and nonce so enqueuer can ack. Example advice payload:```json
{"mode":"FASTPATH","ttl_ms":20000,"nonce":"f1d2c3","reason":"queued_p95_spike","metrics":{"queued_p95":410,"queue_len":310}}
```
sam: important: enqueuer must be able to accept advice and immediately apply a localized strategy: try N fastpath tokens then fallback to SOFT_DROP. Keep it tenant-configurable.
nora: Hysteresis is key. We should re-enable NORMAL only after queued_p95 < 0.6*T for at least 45s, and add exponential backoff on re-trips to avoid oscillation.
eli: Edge-case: FASTPATH reduces KV usage but raises CPU, could worsen packing. We should estimate a simple delta: net_benefit = latency_gain_est - cpu_cost_est, where cpu_cost_est = cpu_per_fastpath_token * tokens_sent. If net_benefit < 0 then prefer EVICT rather than FASTPATH. For MVP we can use conservative defaults (prefer FASTPATH for short windows of 5-10 requests).
hailey: Also design the API to be idempotent and observable: Advice includes nonce + issued_ts, enqueuer replies with ack {nonce, applied_mode, applied_until}. If scheduler restarts, it can re-issue same nonce and enqueuer can dedupe.
sam: Telemetry: emit admission_decision{mode,tenant}, admission_trip_count, admission_time_in_state_seconds, admission_outcome{fastpath_success,fastpath_miss,evict_success,evict_fail,softdrop_served}. Dashboards: per-tenant heatmap of trips and q95.
nora: Safety: Default policy = no HARD_DROP for tier>=enterprise; PLG gets SOFT_DROP allowed but keep lenient thresholds. Admin override via config service flag.
hailey: Rollout plan: feature-flag gated Advice generation; enqueuer will honor advice only if flag enabled per-cluster. Start with a read-only mode where scheduler logs advice without enforcing. Canary at 1 cluster, monitor admission_outcome.
eli: Simulator: I can build a small trace-driven sim that models KV miss bursts, CPU delta and packing waits. We'll sweep S, L, and coefficients a,b,c,d to find stable regions.
sam: Work items: 1) proto for AdmissionAdvice + ack 2) sim + param sweep 3) basic scoring impl in scheduler 4) enqueuer patch + ack path 5) dashboard panels + alerts 6) feature flag rollout plan.
nora: I'll draft the proto and feature flag flow. hailey: I'll own enqueuer changes and canary runbook. eli: simulator + perf tests. sam: I'll wire telemetry and dashboards.
canary-bot: Feature flag "admission-advice" created (env: canary). Ticket INF-4230, INF-4231, INF-4232 created and assigned.
hailey: One more note: make the advice payload intentionally small and mqtt-friendly for low-latency delivery. Also version the proto so future fields can be added.
eli: For thresholds, start with S=1200, L=200, a=1, b=400, c=0.5, d=2 as a conservative point. We'll tune after sim.
sam: OK let's sync Wed 11:30 in eng-runtime to review proto + sim output. Thanks all.
